title: Etale coordinate-subspace models for blowups of smooth pairs
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $P\to S$ and $C\to S$ smooth morphisms, and $i:C\hookrightarrow P$ a closed immersion over $S$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\mathcal I$ be its quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $b:B=\operatorname{Bl}_C(P)\to P$ be the blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Then $\mathcal I$ is of finite type (locally generated by finitely many sections), and $i$ is of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated) [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For every $c\in C$ there exist an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq P$ of $i(c)$, integers $a,b_0\geq0$, and an etale $S$-morphism $h:V\to\mathbf A^{a+b_0}_S$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space] such that $C\times_PV$ is the scheme-theoretic inverse image of the coordinate subspace cut out by the last $b_0$ coordinates. Put $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_a,y_1,\ldots,y_{b_0}]$ and $J=(y_1,\ldots,y_{b_0})$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The ideal $\mathcal I|_V$ is generated by $h^*y_1,\ldots,h^*y_{b_0}$, and the canonical flat-base-change comparisons give isomorphisms over $V$
$$b^{-1}(V)\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_{C\times_PV}(V)\simeq V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Bl}_J(\operatorname{Spec}A)$$
[def-pc-fibre-product, def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map]. In particular, the morphism from $b^{-1}(V)$ to $\operatorname{Bl}_J(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ induced by this comparison and the second projection is etale. The center may be empty or contain whole open components of $P$.

proof.text: Smoothness makes q locally of finite presentation and p locally of finite type. Rewrite i followed by p as q using hi, and apply the proved source-library locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_comp (lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation) to obtain local finite presentation of i. A closed immersion is quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated. This proves the full finite-presentation conjunction without assuming either structure map quasi-compact.

For every affine open W of P, the proved source-library Scheme.Hom.fg_ideal_ker applies to the closed immersion i, now locally of finite presentation. Its proof uses finite presentation of the surjective section map on W and the finite-generation-of-kernel criterion. Thus i.ker.ideal W is finitely generated on every affine open, exactly i.ker.ofFiniteType by ofFiniteType_iff. This works for an empty center and requires no cover argument.

Apply lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates at c and retain V,a,b,h, its etaleness, base compatibility and ideal generators. The regular-sequence and coordinate-square conclusions are not required. The proved flat kernel base-change API Scheme.Hom.ker_of_isPullback for the square defining C times_P V identifies the kernel of its second projection with i.ker.comap V.ι. Therefore the given generators are generators of that restricted ideal.

Compute the inverse image of the existing polynomial center on each affine open W of V. comap_ofIdealTop, ofIdealTop_ideal and Ideal.map_span identify it with the span of the images of the y variables. Naturality of ΓSpecIso and AffineSpace.SpecIso_hom_appTop show that smoothPairPolynomialIso pulls the Sum.inr j variable back to coordinate ULift.up (Fin.natAdd a j). The two spans therefore agree on every affine open, giving equality e of ideal sheaves. The private polynomialIso_coord and center_comap_ideal helpers prove this computation directly.

Choose E1 to be exactly the inverse of blowupFlatBaseChangeFirstIso for the open inclusion and choose E2 to be exactly smoothPairCoordinateBlowupIso with equality e. Flatness holds for the open inclusion and for h composed with the polynomial isomorphism. The upstream blowupFlatBaseChangeIso_hom_snd identity, followed by pullback symmetry, proves that the first-factor comparison is over its source. Cancel its inverse for the E1 projection identity. For E2 compose that same projection identity with ideal-equality transport; the private blowupMap_eqToHom helper proves transport compatibility by equality elimination. These choices meet both fixed-isomorphism equalities literally.

The coordinate map composed with the polynomial isomorphism is etale. Its pullback second projection is etale by lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change. Both E1.hom and E2.hom are isomorphisms, so composition proves the displayed etaleness. No positivity or nonemptiness hypothesis is introduced, and zero coordinate counts and the zero base ring are allowed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N7-e6fec9155 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node and every cited statement in full, against Stacks 0FUE, 0FUT, 0805, 01TV and 02GO. Step 1: lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates works over any base, and its hypotheses (both maps smooth, closed immersion over S) hold exactly; it gives V, a, b_0, h, the inverse-image clause and the generators of I|_V. Step 2: finite type of the ideal is elementary, since off the closed image the ideal is (1). Step 3: the new 01TV node gives finite presentation, including qc/qs. Step 4: def/thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change (I also read the main-20261015 blueprint_update) applies to the open inclusion j and to the étale h : V → A^{a+b_0}_S = Spec A, both flat. The extended ideal is the ideal of the inverse-image subscheme, which is C×_P V in both cases, so both comparisons have source Bl_{C×_P V}(V), with Y as the first factor. Step 5: the 02GO leaf gives the étale second projection, with no circular use of the parent. New node lem-trf-closed-immersion-finite-presentation-ideal: it states 01TV exactly, B1-B7 hold, Mathlib has no scheme-level match (I grepped ClosedImmersion.lean), and the DAG has no duplicate (checked the other 01TV citers and the closed-immersion/finite-presentation ids). It is a genuine lemma and not a clause of the item. Tested on Z empty, Z = X, and a non-finitely-generated ideal of k[x_1, x_2, ...]. Item edge cases: empty center, b_0 = 0 with an empty blowup, arbitrary R. lem-sfb-smooth-coordinate-blowup-charts is field-only and not a duplicate. The two declared tool uses (0FUE coordinates, 0805 comparison) are generic and accepted. No SGA source. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.Hom.smooth_pair_blowup_local_models (R : Type u) [CommRing R] {P C : Scheme.{u}} (p : P ⟶ Spec (.of R)) (q : C ⟶ Spec (.of R)) (i : C ⟶ P) [Smooth p] [Smooth q] [IsClosedImmersion i] (hi : i ≫ p = q) : i.ker.ofFiniteType ∧ (LocallyOfFinitePresentation i ∧ QuasiCompact i ∧ QuasiSeparated i) ∧ ∀ c : C, ∃ (V : P.Opens) (_ : i c ∈ V) (a b : ℕ) (h : V.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (a + b))) (Spec (.of R))) (hEtale : Etale h) (e : i.ker.comap V.ι = (CoordinateSubspaceBlowup.center R a b).comap (h ≫ (smoothPairPolynomialIso R a b).hom)), h ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (a + b))) (Spec (.of R)) ↘ Spec (.of R)) = V.ι ≫ p ∧ (∀ W : V.toScheme.affineOpens, (i.ker.comap V.ι).ideal W = Ideal.span (Set.range (fun j : Fin b ↦ V.toScheme.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : W.1 ≤ ⊤)).op (h.appTop (AffineSpace.coord (Spec (.of R)) (ULift.up (Fin.natAdd a j))))))) ∧ ∃ E₁ : pullback V.ι i.ker.blowupMap ≅ (i.ker.comap V.ι).blowup, E₁ = (i.ker.blowupFlatBaseChangeFirstIso V.ι).symm ∧ E₁.hom ≫ (i.ker.comap V.ι).blowupMap = pullback.fst V.ι i.ker.blowupMap ∧ ∃ E₂ : (i.ker.comap V.ι).blowup ≅ pullback (h ≫ (smoothPairPolynomialIso R a b).hom) (CoordinateSubspaceBlowup.center R a b).blowupMap, E₂ = smoothPairCoordinateBlowupIso R i.ker V a b h hEtale e ∧ E₂.hom ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = (i.ker.comap V.ι).blowupMap ∧ Etale (E₁.hom ≫ E₂.hom ≫ pullback.snd _ _)
